findings.current: After fighting for hours, they were little better than walking corpses drenched in blood.
findings.defect: “Walking corpses” adds a deathlike condition; the source describes fighters covered in blood.
findings.rationale: 혈인 describes how blood-soaked they have become, not whether they resemble corpses.
findings.replacement: After hours of fighting, they were covered in blood from head to toe.
findings.source: 몇 시진 동안이나 계속된 전투로 혈인(血人)이나 다름없어진 그들은

findings.current: nor the nomads who had once roamed the world with a single lance and bow
findings.defect: “Roamed” loses the nomads’ former martial dominance.
findings.rationale: 천하를 질타했던 evokes formidable power, not merely travel.
findings.replacement: nor the nomads who had once struck fear across the land with lance and bow
findings.source: 한때 한 자루의 돌격창과 활로 천하를 질타했던 유목민들도

findings.current: His hair was bristly as a lazy monk’s shaved head, and so red it seemed to be on fire.
findings.defect: A shaved head obscures the image of a monk who has let his hair grow into stubble.
findings.rationale: 돋아난 머리카락 describes hair growing out, which supplies the joke about the lazy monk.
findings.replacement: His hair had grown into prickly stubble, like a lazy monk’s, and was so red it seemed to be on fire.
findings.source: 마치 게으른 승려의 머리처럼, 까슬까슬하게 돋아난 머리카락이 타오르는 것처럼 붉다.

findings.defect: “Take that back” sounds like an order to someone else, though Taekyung retracts his own offer.
findings.rationale: 방금 했던 말 refers to what Taekyung himself just said.
findings.replacement: No, wait. I take that back.
findings.source: 아니, 아니다. 방금 했던 말 취소.

findings.current: He had neither the internal energy of several jiazi nor the divine presence to stand shoulder to shoulder with them. Yet there was an inexplicable weight to him.
findings.defect: “Divine presence” turns the martial might he lacks into an aspect of bearing, blurring the contrast with his authority.
findings.rationale: 신위 is paired with accumulated internal energy as something the three masters possess; his 위압감 comes from a different source.
findings.replacement: He had neither several jiazi of internal energy nor the godlike power to stand shoulder to shoulder with them. Yet he commanded an inexplicable authority.
findings.source: 비록 수 갑자에 달하는 공력도, 그들과 어깨를 나란히 할 신위(神威)도 없었으나 알 수 없는 위압감이 있다.

findings.current: *“How could we possibly do that? The Second Young Master’s natural martial talent is so extraordinary that we wouldn’t dare lay a hand on his training.”*
findings.defect: The retainer denies being able to guide the child, not merely watching him; “lay a hand on his training” is also misleading.
findings.rationale: This is a deferential correction of the Family Head’s suggestion that they are overseeing the boy’s training.
findings.replacement: *“We could hardly claim to be teaching him. The Second Young Master is so gifted that there’s nothing we dare try to correct.”*
findings.source: 어찌 그러겠습니까. 이공자께서는 타고난 무재가 워낙 뛰어나시니, 속하들로서는 감히 손을 댈 수 없을 지경입니다.

findings.current: *“Yes, of course. How could he not be? Who do you think gave birth to him?”*
findings.defect: The father’s boast about whose son the boy is becomes a question about who physically gave birth to him.
findings.rationale: In context, the Family Head puffs out his chest to claim credit for his son’s talent.
findings.replacement: *“Of course he is. Whose son do you think he is?”*
findings.source: 그래, 당연히 그렇겠지. 누가 낳은 자식인데.

findings.current: *“Of course not. Do I look that oblivious?”*
findings.defect: “Of course not” agrees that he is not unwelcome; the Family Head rejects the retainers’ denial.
findings.rationale: 아니긴 dismisses their “No, of course not,” rather than affirming it.
findings.replacement: *“Don’t give me that. Do I look that oblivious?”*
findings.source: 아니긴. 내가 그리 눈치 없는 사람으로 보이나?

findings.defect: “So that’s fate” adds a conclusion where the father only repeats the word bitterly.
findings.rationale: The repetition precedes his rejection of fate in “It’s all my fault.”

summary: Several lines alter physical details, a father’s joke, and the force of his reply to the retainers.
